name: Durban sugar bean curry
summary: Speckled sugar beans and a little potato simmered in an onion, tomato and curry-leaf masala gravy, served over brown rice with a sharp carrot, tomato and cucumber kachumbar.
about: Sugar beans, the speckled pink beans sold dried and tinned in South African shops, are cooked as a curry in Durban's Indian homes as a meal without meat: braised with whole spices and curry leaves, then simmered in a tomato and masala gravy, often with potato. It goes to the table with rice or roti and a vinegary onion salad called kachumbar.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.note: medium, about 300 g, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

steps: Put the rice and water in a saucepan with a tight lid and bring to the boil over high heat. Turn the heat to low and cook, covered, for 40 minutes, until the water is absorbed and the grains are tender. Leave it covered off the heat.
For the kachumbar, toss the onion, tomato, carrot and cucumber with the vinegar, salt, pepper and coriander. Cover and chill while the curry cooks; the vinegar takes the sharp edge off the raw onion.

Heat the oil in a large heavy-based pot over medium heat. Add the mustard seeds and, as soon as they start to pop, the cumin seeds, fenugreek seeds and cinnamon. Stir for about 20 seconds, until the cumin darkens a shade; fenugreek turns bitter if it burns, so do not leave the pot.
Add the onion, curry leaves and green chilli and fry, stirring now and then, for 8 to 10 minutes, until the onion is soft and golden at the edges. Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the masala, ground coriander, ground cumin and turmeric and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant, adding a spoon of water if the spices start to catch.
Add the grated tomatoes and the salt and cook, stirring, for 6 to 8 minutes, until they have cooked down to a thick, dark paste and the oil gathers at the edges.
Add the potatoes and the 375 ml water and stir to coat them in the paste. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until a knife goes into the potato with only a little resistance.

Add the sugar beans and simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring gently and crushing a few beans against the side of the pot, until the potato is soft and the gravy is thick enough to coat the beans. Add a splash of water if it gets too dry.
Take out the cinnamon stick, taste for salt and scatter with the coriander. Serve over the brown rice with the kachumbar on the side.
prepNote: The curry keeps 3 days in the fridge and freezes well; loosen it with water when reheating. Make the kachumbar on the day.
